podcast.title: Early Independent Alternative Label
podcast.body: SST was listed as one of the small, independent, niche record companies that began to emerge in the late 1970s and early 1980s. These labels offered "an alternative to the majors" by focusing on signing and distributing groups that had been influenced by the creative and attitudinal impact of punk rock. "These labels, which had names like Epitaph, ST, Berserkerly, Rounder, Sire and dozens of others, provided an alternative to the majors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Operations and Management
podcast.body: In its initial stages, all operations for SST Records were handled directly by members of Black Flag—specifically the guitarist and bassist—along with two roadies. This highly hands-on approach characterized the label's early independence. "Everything was handled by the guitarist, the bass player, and two roadies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Release: Nervous Breakdown
podcast.body: The first release on SST was Black Flag's EP titled "Nervous Breakdown" in 1979. "The first release on the label was a Black Flag EP entitled Nervous Breakdown in 1979."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation by Black Flag Members
podcast.body: SST was founded by Black Flag's Greg Ginn, who also owned a ham radio electronics company called Solid State Tuners, and bass player Chuck Dukowski. The label was formed to release Black Flag's debut EP, "Nervous Breakdown," after the band failed to secure a record deal elsewhere. "Greg Ginn, the founder of the band, which had come together in 1977 under the name Panic, had a side hustle selling ham radio electronics through the mail. He called his company Solid State Tuners. When the group couldn't get anyone to put out the record, Greg and bass player Chuck Dukowski formed SST, which is short for Solid State Tuners."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founded by Black Flag
podcast.body: SST Records was established by the punk band Black Flag as a "do it yourself" initiative. They formed their own label after major record labels in Hollywood showed no interest in signing them, believing punk was a fad. "So in true, do it yourself, Sphere, the flag formed their own record label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founded by Greg Ginn for Black Flag
podcast.body: SST was founded by guitarist Greg Ginn in 1978, originally as an electronic components mail-order company established in 1966 when he was 12. Ginn repurposed it into a record label specifically to distribute material from his band, Black Flag, because no other label would work with them. "He'd started the company in 1966 when he was just 12 and the purpose was to sell electronic components through the mail. But in 1978, he turned it into a record label to distribute material from his band because no other label wanted to touch what they were doing."

podcast.title: Founding by Black Flag Members
podcast.body: SST was founded by Black Flag's Greg Ginn and Chuck Dukowski in January 1979. The name is short for Solid State Tuners, which was Greg Ginn's side business selling ham radio electronics. The label was created to release Black Flag's debut EP, "Nervous Breakdown," after they couldn't find a label to put it out. "Greg Ginn, the founder of the band, which had come together in 1977 under the name Panic, had a side hustle selling ham radio electronics through the mail. He called his company Solid State Tuners. When the group couldn't get anyone to put out the record, Greg and bass player Chuck Dukowski formed SST, which is short for Solid State Tuners."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hardcore Spreader
podcast.body: Beyond Black Flag, SST was instrumental in spreading hardcore music from numerous other groups, including The Minutemen and The Meat Puppets. The label's output of hardcore records increased in popularity and widespread distribution as Ronald Reagan's presidency continued. "Not only did SST release flag records, they were also too happy to spread hardcore from groups like The Minutemen, The Meat Puppets, and dozens of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Husker Dew's Former Label
podcast.body: Husker Dew was an independent band that transitioned from SST Records to Warner Brothers, making them an early example of an indie act signing with a major label. "Now, Husker Dew had done it, jumping from SST to Warner Brothers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Origin
podcast.body: The label was named SST after an old electronic company, reflecting a utilitarian, no-frills approach consistent with the punk ethos. "They called it SST after an old electronic company."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneering Independent Label
podcast.body: SST was one of the small independent labels that specialized in releasing music outside the traditional major label system during the post-punk indie movement. "that included rough trade for a D, beggars banquet, epitaph, SST, and many others."

podcast.title: Punk Hero Roster
podcast.body: SST Records, a prominent California independent label, was known for releasing albums by influential 80s punk heroes such as The Minutemen, Black Flag, and Husker Dü. Soundgarden signed with SST after their initial releases on Sub Pop. "SST Records, which had issued albums by such 80s punk heroes as The Minute Men, Black Flag, and Husker Do."

podcast.title: Ray Farrell's Transition to DGC/Geffen
podcast.body: Ray Farrell, who previously worked with SST Records, later moved to DGC/Geffen Records, contributing to DGC's reputation as a "unicorn label" among majors for its somewhat independent approach. "Ray Farrell from SST Records who we were recording with, he's working there now."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Release of Hüsker Dü Records
podcast.body: SST Records released a series of records by Hüsker Dü before the band signed with a major label, Warner Records. This underscores SST's role in nurturing influential indie bands. "Husker Do found a lot of love on college radio and after a series of records, some of which Ron Blackfags' SST label"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spreading Indie Influence
podcast.body: SST Records, an indie label associated with Black Flag, played a crucial role in allowing bands like Sonic Youth and Husker Dew to spread their influence throughout North America. "Although Sonic Youth's music became more structured as the 80s progressed, there was always the sense that they were pushing the edge of the musical envelope and thanks to a deal with black flags, indie label, SST records, they were able to spread their influence throughout North America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Spreading Sonic Youth's Influence
podcast.body: SST Records played a crucial role in expanding the reach and influence of New York's Sonic Youth, distributing their music and helping them spread their sound throughout North America. "And thanks to a deal with Black Flag's SSD records, they were able to spread their influence throughout North America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Success Despite Challenges
podcast.body: Despite early struggles, including a near-fatal legal battle with a major label, SST Records eventually mastered the business of running an independent company and achieved considerable success. "Black Flag struggled for a few years, almost losing a legal battle with a major label that would have killed both the band and their label, but eventually they got the hang of running an independent company and did quite well."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
